{"id":"814b77e8-399b-4a6e-a737-5c18762a3d72","object":"chat.completion","created":1790516974,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"support_claim_ids": ["C3", "C5"]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer identify which current verified claims provide substantive evidentiary support for fixed Parent Requirement. Parent Requirement: "A pack of downloadable content was released for a strategy video game over three years after its release." Need support claims that establish DLC released for strategy video game over three years after its release. We have claims.

Need determine which claims substantively support R1. R1 requires: a pack of downloadable content was released for a strategy video game over three years after its release. Need establish DLC, for strategy video game, release date, base game release date, difference >3 years. Claims:

C1 thesis irrelevant to R1 except identifies game? No release. Not support.
C2 advisor irrelevant.
C3: DLC 'Expansion - Europa Universalis IV: Rights of Man' for EU4 released on 11 Oct 2016. This establishes DLC for EU4 and release date of DLC.
C4: wiki page details dev diaries, changes. Not release date relation.
C5: EU4 is a 2013 grand strategy video game; released 25 Aug 2013 (Wikipedia body) or 13 Aug 2013 infobox. This establishes base game strategy video game and release date 2013.
C6: manual tech changes. Not support for R1.
C7: manual changes. Not support.
C8: credits content designers. Not support R1.
C9: third content designer. Not support R1.

To support R1, need combine C3 and C5. C3 says DLC for EU4 released 11 Oct 2016. C5 says EU4 is strategy game released 2013. Together they establish DLC released over three years after base release? Let's check dates: 2013-08-13 to 2016-10-11 = over 3 years? 2016-08-13 is 3 years. Oct 11 2016 > Aug 13 2016, so over 3 years (by ~2 months). If use Aug 25, also over 3 years? 2016-08-25 + 3 years? 2016-08-25 is 3 years after Aug 25 2013; Oct 11 after. So yes. But do we count both C3 and C5 as substantive support? The question asks which current Verified Claims provide substantive evidentiary support for one fixed Parent Requirement. A claim counts as substantive support only when Claim itself establishes material part of Parent Requirement with required entities etc. C3 establishes DLC for strategy video game? It says for Europa Universalis IV. It does not itself state EU4 is strategy video game or release date. But C5 establishes EU4 is strategy video game and release date. C3 establishes DLC release date. Neither alone fully establishes R1; but each establishes material part. The instructions: "You identify which current Verified Claims provide substantive evidentiary support for one fixed Parent Requirement." Could be multiple claims together. Need return IDs. They ask "Do NOT count a Claim as support merely because ..." They don't forbid partial support. Examples: "a memorandum date does not establish the date of a different enclosed letter" implies partial might not count if not establishing required relation. But for R1, C3 and C5 are both material parts. C3: DLC released for EU4. C5: EU4 is strategy game with release date. These together prove R1. Do we include both? Likely yes. But let's examine if C3 alone: "The downloadable content 'Expansion - Europa Universalis IV: Rights of Man' for Europa Universalis IV was released on 11 October 2016." It explicitly states downloadable content for Europa Universalis IV. It doesn't state EU4 is strategy video game or base release. C5: "Europa Universalis IV is a 2013 grand strategy video game; ... released on 25 August 2013..." This states game, genre, release. So C5 provides strategy video game and release year/date. C3 provides DLC release and game. Together.

Question: "You identify which current Verified Claims provide substantive evidentiary support for one fixed Parent Requirement." The parent requirement is exactly "A pack of downloadable content was released for a strategy video game over three years after its release." So support claims should be those that directly establish this. C3 and C5 combined do. C3 alone doesn't establish strategy or >3 years. C5 alone doesn't establish DLC. But both are necessary. If we only return claims that individually fully support, none. But that seems too strict? The instruction: "A Claim counts as SUBSTANTIVE SUPPORT only when the Claim itself establishes a material part of the Parent Requirement..." So partial is allowed if material part. "with the required entity, participant role, relation direction, object, temporal attachment, event/document binding, and candidate branch." This suggests a claim must establish material part with correct entities. C3 establishes DLC for EU4 with release date. C5 establishes EU4 is strategy video game with release date. Both are material parts. So include C3 and C5. What about C9? It establishes third content designer but for the overall original question, not Parent Requirement R1. R1 only about DLC release over 3 years. C9 not support R1. C8/C9 relate to answer but not parent requirement. C1/C2 relate thesis. C4/C6/C7 relate mechanics changes. Not R1.

Could C3 alone be enough if we already know EU4 is strategy video game from outside? But we can't use outside. We have C5. So both.

Check dates: C3 release 11 Oct 2016. C5 release 2013 (either 13 or 25 Aug 2013). Difference over three years? If base release 25 Aug 2013, 11 Oct 2016 is 3 years 1.5 months. If 13 Aug, 3 years 2 months. Yes. So C3 and C5 together establish R1. But does C5 "a 2013 grand strategy video game" and "released on 25 August 2013" establish strategy video game? Yes.

Thus support_claim_ids: ["C3","C5"]. Need return JSON only. Ensure no extra text.
